blurbEn: You will be able to explain exactly what the three CIPLE components are, what each one is worth, what score you need, and where your twelve weeks of study should go.
notePrompt: Teach the shape of the exam before any Portuguese. CIPLE is the Certificado Inicial de Português Língua Estrangeira, the A2 exam of CAPLE at the Faculdade de Letras da Universidade de Lisboa; CAPLE's own FAQ calls A2 the minimum level for acquiring Portuguese nationality, and Portaria n.º 1403-A/2006, art. 1.º n.º 2, fixes A2 as 'conhecimento suficiente em língua portuguesa'. Three components are sat on one day: Compreensão da Leitura e Produção e Interação Escritas, 1h15, 45%; Compreensão do Oral, 30 minutes, 30%; Produção e Interação Orais, about 15 minutes for a PAIR of candidates, 25% — roughly two hours in total plus a 15-minute break. The pass is 55% of the weighted total (0,45 x leitura/escrita + 0,30 x compreensão do oral + 0,25 x produção oral); the bands are Suficiente 55-69%, Bom 70-84%, Muito Bom 85-100%, and below 55% CAPLE's FAQ uses the label Insuficiente and issues a Comunicação de Resultados instead of a certificate. Say honestly that CAPLE publishes NO minimum per component — preparation sites claim 25% or 45%, they contradict each other and none of them cites CAPLE — so the safe rule is to aim for 55% in every component and never plan to sacrifice one. Do the weighting arithmetic out loud: reading plus writing is almost half the exam and is the most trainable part for an adult who already lives in Portugal, so it earns the most hours. Give the shape of the twelve weeks: week 0 secure the exam seat, weeks 1-2 diagnose and rebuild the A2 spine, weeks 3-7 reading and writing, weeks 6-9 listening, weeks 8-11 the paired oral, week 12 full timed mocks. Warn once, inventing nothing: since 19 May 2026 nationality also requires knowledge of culture, history, national symbols (Lei Orgânica n.º 1/2026, art. 6.º n.º 1 al. c) and of rights, duties and political organisation (al. d); nationals of Portuguese-speaking countries are presumed to satisfy only the LANGUAGE part of c); and as of August 2026 the implementing regulation for that civics test had not been published, so its format, price and dates are unknown and must never be stated. Mention that a school version, CIPLE-e, exists for ages 12-15.

blurbEn: You will be able to sit CAPLE's published model papers under the real clock, score yourself with the real weighting, and name the component that is costing you the pass.
notePrompt: This unit is a procedure, not a lesson: the learner gets a real baseline in week 1, before studying anything. CAPLE publishes a free model set — the reading and writing paper (6 pages), the listening paper (4 pages), a 30-minute audio file and a single answer key covering both papers; there is NO published model for the oral component, so that one is rehearsed with a partner instead. Instruct them to sit the written paper with a pencil, a blue or black pen and a 75-minute timer, take a 15-minute break, then play the listening audio from start to finish without pausing: the audio is exactly thirty minutes long and IS the component, so there is no reading time before it and no extra time after it. Scoring: 20 reading items plus 2 written texts in the first paper, 25 items in the listening; turn each component into a percentage, then compute the weighted total 0,45 / 0,30 / 0,25 and compare it with 55%. Give the landmarks but flag the assumption: about 14 of 25 listening items is roughly 55% of that component and about 18 of 25 is roughly 70%, on the assumption of equal item weighting, which CAPLE does not publish. Make them write down three numbers, one per component, and the two worst task types by name, because everything after this unit is triage. Be honest that the two written texts cannot be self-scored objectively — CAPLE publishes no marking grid for them — so judge them only against what the paper itself demands: the word count, the addressee and every instruction in the prompt. Tell them to repeat the whole run in week 12, and to do the listening after 75 minutes of written work rather than fresh, because that is the real condition on the day.

titleEn: Counters and Services: the Ten Places
titlePt: Balcões e Serviços: Os Dez Espaços
blurbEn: You will be able to tell, from a single overheard sentence, which counter or public service you are standing at — and say the five phrases you need there.
notePrompt: Build this unit on the ten espaços de comunicação that CAPLE's own listening paper uses in Parte 2, because that list is published and verbatim: escola, táxi, mercado, centro de saúde, agência de emprego, consulado/embaixada, restaurante, correios, aeroporto, loja de produtos informáticos. For each place teach the five things you would hear ONLY there — correios: selo, carta registada, encomenda, levantar, código postal; centro de saúde: marcar uma consulta, receita, tenho dores, número de utente, análises; agência de emprego: candidatura, currículo, entrevista, contrato, a tempo inteiro; consulado ou embaixada: visto, autorização de residência, senha, impresso, passaporte; aeroporto: embarque, bagagem de mão, porta, atraso, cartão de embarque; táxi: leve-me a…, pode parar aqui, o troco, praça de táxis; mercado: um quilo de, quanto é o quilo?, está fresco?, mais alguma coisa?; restaurante: a ementa, o prato do dia, a conta, uma bica; escola: a aula, o horário, os trabalhos de casa, a inscrição; loja de informática: garantia, carregador, ecrã, avariado, talão. Flag the counter words that decide whole exam items: senha is the numbered queue ticket and not a password, impresso is a form to fill in, visto is a visa, talão de compra is the receipt, trocar and devolver are what you do with a faulty purchase, renda and arrendar belong to housing. Teach the transaction frame as one block, since it is reused in the oral role-play: 'Bom dia. Queria…, se faz favor', 'Quanto é?', 'Pode ajudar-me?', 'Onde é que fica…?', 'Tenho de trazer mais alguma coisa?', 'Posso trocar isto?'. Point out how immigrant-shaped the official list is — agência de emprego, consulado, centro de saúde — and that this same vocabulary reappears in the reading notices and in the oral simulation, so it is paid for three times. Insist on the European forms throughout: autocarro, comboio, paragem, telemóvel, casa de banho, pequeno-almoço, empregado de mesa, sumo, ementa, frigorífico, talho, multibanco, morada, apelido. Drill it as 'o que se diz onde': give one sentence and ask for the place, then reverse it and ask for a sentence that could only be said there.

blurbEn: You will be able to read a Portuguese public notice or classified ad at speed and answer the one question that turns on a single word.
notePrompt: This is pure exam lexicon and it is the highest-yield vocabulary in the whole CIPLE, because five reading items are built directly on it and the same words come back in the listening. Teach the notice set as a closed list: dias úteis, horário de atendimento, horário contínuo, encerra, encerrado, feriados, marcação prévia, visitas guiadas, preço especial, prazo, a partir de, até, destinatários, local, documentos necessários, avariado, proibido, obras, aviso, senha. Then the classified-ad set: arrenda-se (the Portuguese verb — aluga-se is Brazilian), T2, mobilado, varanda, zona comercial, renda, oferece-se, procuro trabalho, televendas, carta de condução de ligeiros, carro próprio, currículo, em anexo. The genres attested on CAPLE's own paper are an apartment ad, an opening-hours notice for the Serviços de Identificação Civil, a museum notice, a job ad and a school-enrolment notice laid out under DESTINATÁRIOS, PRAZO, LOCAL and DOCUMENTOS NECESSÁRIOS (cartão de cidadão e boletim de vacinas) — reproduce that shape when you write practice items. Make the two mechanical skills explicit, because both appear: comparing two rows of the same timetable (Lisboa das 8h30 às 19h30 contra Porto das 9h00 às 16h00) and converting a condition into a true-or-false claim (todas as crianças nascidas no ano de 2007). Teach the trap the real model contains: an ad headed EMPREGO: OFERECE-SE whose body reads 'Procuro trabalho na área de televendas' — the writer wants work, and a candidate who answers from the heading instead of the text loses the item. Add the institutional nouns that also serve the nationality process: Cartão de Cidadão, boletim de vacinas, Serviços de Identificação Civil, Centro de Emprego, junta de freguesia, atestado de residência, comprovativo de morada. Drill by handing over a notice plus one three-option question and requiring the learner to point at the exact words that make each option true or false; if they cannot find the words, it is not the answer.

blurbEn: You will be able to catch a time, a price, a floor and a turning first time, at Portuguese speed, and write them down without a replay.
grammarFocus: numerais cardinais e ordinais; expressões de tempo, de lugar e de direção
notePrompt: Sell this unit as the cheapest marks in the exam: whole listening items are decided by two seconds of audio — 14h30 against 18h30, or '1.º andar, 2.ª porta à direita' against 'à esquerda'. Teach the European numerals explicitly against the Brazilian ones most learners arrive with: catorze (not quatorze), dezasseis, dezassete, dezanove (not dezesseis, dezessete, dezenove). Cover the clock both ways, because the exam uses both: às seis e meia, às seis e um quarto, um quarto para as sete, dezoito e trinta, meio-dia, meia-noite, da manhã, da tarde, da noite. Teach the time expressions that carry rules rather than just times: quinze dias means a fortnight, daqui a uma semana, na semana seguinte à compra, dias úteis, ao fim de semana, dentro de uma hora, há dois anos for elapsed time. Money next: quanto é?, quanto custa?, dois euros e cinquenta, vinte e cinco euros, o troco, o talão, multibanco, levantar dinheiro, pagar a pronto. Directions and position are a guaranteed topic in both the listening and the oral: rés-do-chão, primeiro andar, segundo andar, à direita, à esquerda, em frente, ao lado de, ao fundo de, no meio de, por baixo de, por cima de, em frente de, junto a, no fim das escadas, vire à direita, siga em frente, atravesse a rua, apanhe o autocarro na paragem. Anchor the whole lot on two verbs that make these answerable in speech: ficar for location ('a farmácia fica ao lado do hotel') and haver ('há um multibanco ao fundo da rua'). Prescribe the drill and say why it works: five minutes a day of ten spoken numbers, times, prices and floor-plus-side directions, written down with no replay — dictation exposes exactly what a feeling of 'understanding' hides.

titleEn: The House, the Furniture and the Professions
titlePt: A Casa, a Mobília e as Profissões
blurbEn: You will be able to describe a photograph of a room or a family for two minutes, and say which job you would like and why.
grammarFocus: preposições de lugar e o imperfeito de cortesia (gostava de + infinitivo)
notePrompt: This unit exists because of one repeatedly reported fact: furniture and the rooms of a house are the vocabulary that catches CIPLE candidates out, since the oral has been reported to hand each candidate a different photograph to describe for about two minutes — an empty kitchen, a furnished room, a family dining in a restaurant. Teach the divisions of the house (sala, cozinha, quarto, casa de banho, corredor, varanda, garagem, sótão, cave) with the furniture and appliances (sofá, poltrona, mesa, cadeira, armário, estante, cómoda, cama, mesa de cabeceira, candeeiro, tapete, cortinas, frigorífico, fogão, forno, micro-ondas, máquina de lavar a loiça). Insist on the European items as you go: frigorífico not geladeira, casa de banho not banheiro, ecrã not tela, telemóvel not celular. Bolt the prepositions of place straight onto the nouns, because a description is nouns plus positions and nothing else: 'à esquerda está o frigorífico', 'à direita está o fogão', 'no meio há uma mesa de madeira com quatro cadeiras', 'o sofá está ao lado da janela', 'por cima da mesa há um candeeiro'. Give a description skeleton to memorise and reuse for any image: 'Nesta fotografia vejo…', then left/right/middle, then what people are doing — always estar a + infinitivo, so 'estão a jantar' and 'estão a conversar', never the Brazilian gerund — then 'Parecem contentes' and 'Acho que é…'. Then teach professions, because a published task hands the pair a sheet of five (polícia, bombeiro, professor, taxista, enfermeiro) and asks which they would choose: add médico, cozinheiro, empregado de mesa, motorista, canalizador, eletricista, agricultor, informático, reformado, desempregado. Drill the opinion frame in the imperfeito de cortesia, which is the A2 politeness workhorse: 'Gostava de ser enfermeira, porque gosto de ajudar as pessoas' and 'Não gostava de ser polícia, porque é um trabalho perigoso e as horas são difíceis'.

blurbEn: You will be able to run the whole A2 grammar checklist and say, for each item, whether you can produce it or only recognise it.
grammarFocus: o núcleo gramatical do A2 — presente, pretérito perfeito simples, pretérito imperfeito, perífrases verbais e colocação dos clíticos
notePrompt: Open by saying plainly that CAPLE publishes no official programa, no grammar list and no wordlist for the CIPLE: this checklist is reconstructed from the Referencial Camões PLE (2017), the QECR A2 descriptors and, above all, from what CAPLE's own sample papers actually contain. Verbs are the level itself: presente do indicativo, regular and irregular; pretérito perfeito simples as the narrative workhorse (cheguei, apanhei, disseram, teve, ficou, resolveram); pretérito imperfeito for background and description (estava, tinha, era, podia); and the imperfeito de cortesia taught as a politeness formula before it is taught as a tense — 'Queria um café, se faz favor', 'Gostava de trabalhar aqui'. Drill the perífrases as single units, because they carry more A2 meaning than any conjugation table: ir + infinitivo for the future (vou ler, vamos ver), estar a + infinitivo for the progressive — 'estou a falar', NEVER 'estou falando', which is Brazilian and reads as a register failure — plus ter de + infinitivo for obligation, acabar de, começar a, continuar a and conseguir + infinitivo. Teach 'há' for elapsed time, because it appears in the oral every single time: 'Vivo em Portugal há três anos', 'Estudo português há dois anos', 'Ficou desempregada há seis meses'. Clitic placement is a first-class A2 topic in Portugal: enclisis by default in affirmative main clauses (chamo-me, dá-me, disseram-lhes, avariou-se) and proclisis after negation, after 'que' and after certain adverbs (não me telefones, que te enviei, já se foi embora); the classic stumble is telefona-me turning into não me telefones. Add the written traps attested on the paper: 'Já chegámos' with the acute accent that marks the past in Portugal, and the Acordo Ortográfico spellings as applied here — ativa, eletrónica, aspeto, but contacto and facto keep their c. Drill the rubric imperatives as exam-survival vocabulary, since a candidate who cannot decode them cannot sit the paper: Leia, Escreva, Faça, Responda, Identifique, Escolha, Marque, Use. Close on connectors, because two linked simple sentences beat one ambitious broken one at A2: porque, mas, e, depois, também, por isso, quando, além disso, uma vez que.

titlePt: Compreensão da Leitura: As Quatro Tarefas
blurbEn: You will be able to recognise all four reading tasks on sight and attack each one with the right technique instead of reading everything twice.
notePrompt: Parte 1 of the 75-minute paper is exactly 20 items in four tasks of five, all marked in pencil on the folha de respostas. Tarefa A, questions 1-5: a one-line situation is matched to one of three SMS-style telemóvel messages; every distractor is a plausible message about the same topic, so what really decides it is who is speaking, to whom, and when — already arrived against still travelling, asking against thanking. Tarefa B, questions 6-10: five short authentic notices and ads, one three-option question each (an apartment ad, a public-service opening-hours notice, a museum notice, a job ad, a school enrolment notice); answer from the words on the page and never from world knowledge, because the published model contains an ad headed EMPREGO: OFERECE-SE whose correct answer is that the writer is looking for work. Tarefa C, questions 11-15: a matching task over a formal carta de candidatura a emprego — five sentence stems in coluna A against EIGHT options in coluna B, each usable once, so exactly three are never used; teach elimination, cross options off as they are committed, and check that precisely three are left over, because the distractors are deliberate mirrors ('os pais ainda não estavam cá' against 'os pais já cá viviam há alguns anos'). Tarefa D, questions 16-20: one longer narrative or journalistic text of roughly 300 words with five three-option questions that follow the order of the text; in the model they turn on cause and motive rather than bare facts, and on reported speech ('disseram-lhes que…'). Teach one universal technique for all four: for every option, put a finger on the words in the text that make it true or false — if you cannot find them, it is not the answer. Nothing in CAPLE's model, key or Normas mentions negative marking, so never leave an item blank; with three options a guess is worth a third of a mark and costs nothing anyone can find. Mention honestly that CAPLE's older published specification also lists verdadeiro/falso items, which do not appear in the current model — spend ten minutes on them so they cannot surprise anyone, and no more.

blurbEn: You will be able to produce both CIPLE written texts to length, in the right register, from a skeleton you can write out from memory.
grammarFocus: pretérito perfeito simples e 'estava a + infinitivo' na narração; tratamento informal no plural (vocês, o vosso, convosco)
notePrompt: Parte 2 of the written paper is two texts and nothing else, and they are very different tasks. Texto 1 is written INTERACTION of 25-35 words: the model has friends texting 'Já chegámos. Estamos à tua espera no café do parque. Ainda demoras?', so the reply must actually answer the direct question with a time; the instruction reads 'deve ter uma extensão de 25-35 palavras', with no 'cerca de', so treat that range as exact. Texto 2 is written PRODUCTION of about 60-80 words: an informal email to friends whose opening line is supplied — 'Caros Amigos, Queria muito estar convosco no fim de semana, mas não consegui' — and the task is to narrate what went wrong, which forces pretérito perfeito simples for the events plus 'estava a + infinitivo' for the background. Both texts go to friends in the PLURAL, so the forms are vocês, o vosso, convosco, esperem, desculpem; warn that the exam's own instructions address the candidate as 'Você marcou um encontro…' and that mirroring 'você' back into a message to friends is wrong-footed in Portugal. Give two skeletons to memorise: Texto 1 — apologise, give the reason, give the time, close ('Olá! Desculpem o atraso. Perdi o autocarro e estou à espera do próximo. Estou a chegar daqui a vinte minutos. Até já!'); Texto 2 — apologise, narrate two or three things in order, close forward-looking ('Na sexta-feira à noite, o carro avariou-se… No sábado, a minha filha ficou doente… Peço imensa desculpa. Espero que possamos combinar outro fim de semana em breve. Um abraço,'). Three mechanical rules void otherwise perfect Portuguese: the texts must be on the folha de respostas in blue or black pen, since answers in pencil or left on the rascunho are not marked at all; the candidate may never write their real name anywhere on the exam, which annuls it, so choose one invented signing name and always practise with it; and the supplied opening of Texto 2 is a stimulus, not word count, so write 60-80 words of your own. Teach word-count control physically — learn what 30 and 70 words look like in your own handwriting, count one full line and multiply, and do it once at the end, not while writing. Be honest that CAPLE publishes no marking grid for these texts, so the only certain criteria are the instructions printed on the paper: word count, task, addressee — and the safe style is short, clear, correct sentences joined with porque, mas, depois, também and por isso, not ambitious ones that multiply errors.

blurbEn: You will be able to walk into the biggest paper with a minute-by-minute plan, so that the reading never eats your writing.
notePrompt: The structural flaw of this paper is that 20 reading items sit in front of the two written texts with no bell between them, so the commonest way to lose 45% of the exam is to write Texto 2 in the last six minutes, or not at all. Give the plan and make the learner rehearse it under a timer at least three times: minutes 0-2, check the folha de respostas, the pencil, the eraser and the blue or black pen; 2-9, questions 1-5; 9-20, questions 6-10; 20-31, questions 11-15; 31-43, questions 16-20; a HARD STOP at minute 43 to verify every pencil mark and fill every blank with a guess; 46-56, Texto 1; 56-71, Texto 2 with roughly three minutes planning, nine writing and three checking; 71-75, count the words of both texts and sweep. Teach the physical switch as a ritual: put the pencil down and pick the pen up before Texto 1, because candidates who carry the pencil across from Parte 1 write an unmarkable text. Offer the legitimate alternative for anyone who panics about time — write Parte 2 first while fresh, then do the reading tired — and say clearly that the point is having a plan, not which of the two you pick. The final sweep is targeted, not a re-read: agreement of gender and number, then verb endings, then accents, then legibility, in that order, because ambiguous handwriting is simply read as an error. Remind them that candidates may not leave the room before the scheduled end, so there is never a reason to stop checking. Set the practice protocol: three timed runs of the whole paper, at least one on real paper with a real pen rather than a screen, scored on one question only — did the plan hold, and was Texto 2 finished with time to check it?

titlePt: Compreensão do Oral: 25 Questões em 30 Minutos
blurbEn: You will be able to work the listening paper the way it is actually built — pre-reading fast, marking as you go, and transferring 25 answers without a slip.
notePrompt: The listening component is 30 minutes, 25 items, four printed pages, two parts, and 30% of the exam — and CAPLE's own audio is exactly thirty minutes long, so the recording IS the component: no reading time before it, no extra time after it. Parte 1 is ten short texts carrying fifteen three-option items, with one or two questions per text and the paper telling you which; the content is transactional, and in the model it runs through a diet interview, a comment on qualifications and work, directions inside a building, two friends at the pool, a shop exchange and its returns rule, a counter conversation about a visto and a senha, buying a coach ticket to Faro, a job application needing an impresso and a copy of the passaporte, directions to the correios, and living inside against outside the city. Parte 2 is 'O que se diz onde': ten heard sentences matched to ten espaços de comunicação lettered A to J; in CAPLE's published key every letter is used exactly once, so teach elimination and crossing off — but say honestly that the rubric does not print that rule, so it is a strong working assumption and a checking tool, not permission to stop listening. Everything is played TWICE with a beep between the two hearings: use the first for gist and for locking onto what the question wants, the second for the one detail that separates two options. The real constraint is time, not difficulty: measured on CAPLE's audio there are only about nine seconds to read the questions before each text and about fourteen seconds to finish afterwards, so pre-reading must be automatic — read the stem and the first three words of each option, which is enough to know whether you are listening for a time, a floor, a rule or a preference. Flag the discrepancy openly: the printed model says 'tem 1 minuto para ler as questões' but no such gap exists anywhere in the audio, so prepare for the tight version and treat anything more generous as a gift. Mark answers on the question paper in pencil as you go, then use the final five and a half minutes of silence to transfer in blocks of five, reading item numbers as you go, because one skipped line shifts every answer after it. Never leave a blank — there is no published negative marking, and in Parte 2 elimination makes a guess worth far more than one in three. Finally, teach how the wrong options are built: the distractor usually repeats words you definitely heard while the key paraphrases them, so an option that sounds like a transcript should be suspected; expect one-detail swaps (right floor, wrong door), two times spoken in the same text, negation and modality carrying the answer (não pode, tem de, apenas, não é preciso), and stems that ask what the speaker thinks rather than what is true.

titleEn: Training Your Ear for European Portuguese
blurbEn: You will be able to hear the sounds European Portuguese swallows, and stop losing marks to pronunciation rather than to words you do not know.
grammarFocus: redução vocálica, ligação de palavras e ênclise dos pronomes na fala
notePrompt: The reason a competent A2 learner fails the listening paper is almost never vocabulary — it is that spoken European Portuguese deletes what the page shows. Teach four mechanisms with examples the learner repeats aloud. First, unstressed vowels reduce and often disappear: telemóvel sounds like 'tlemóvel', pequeno-almoço like 'p'quen'almoç', perguntar like 'prguntar', desculpe like 'd'sculp', está a chover like 'tá-a-chvêr'. Second, final and pre-consonantal s sounds like 'sh', turns into a 'zh' before a voiced consonant (dois dias, desde), and links as 'z' across a word gap before a vowel, so 'os amigos' arrives as one ribbon of sound, 'uzamigush', and word boundaries vanish. Third, est- collapses: estar, está bem becomes 'tá bem', and combined with the linking rule 'está a estudar' arrives as a single cluster — which is also the construction Brazilian input never trains, because pt-PT uses estar a + infinitivo and never the gerund. Fourth, syllable-final l is dark and close to a 'w' (Portugal, papel, hotel, mil) while final r is weak, so infinitives blur. Add the grammar the ear must expect: enclitic pronouns (chamo-me, diga-me, sente-se, pode ajudar-me) put the pronoun exactly where a Brazilian-trained learner expects the next word. Drill nasals as meaning-bearing, since negation lives inside one — não pode against pode decides real items — and tem against têm are near-identical in speech, so number comes from context. Prescribe the routine: ten minutes of pt-PT dictation daily (thirty to sixty seconds of authentic audio written out, then checked), five minutes of numbers, times and prices, one-listen comprehension three times a week to build margin over the exam's two hearings, and shadowing twice a week, because producing the reductions is the mechanism that makes them audible. Input must be Portuguese from Portugal — RTP, Antena 1, TSF, Rádio Renascença, and radio phone-ins or street interviews rather than newsreaders, who are too clean — and tell the learner plainly to stop using Brazilian audio in the last two months: not because it is worse Portuguese, but because it trains the wrong vowels, the wrong progressive and the wrong pronoun position. Finish with the discourse padding, so it becomes wallpaper instead of noise: pronto, pois, ora bem, já agora, se faz favor, com certeza, está bem, não faz mal, olhe, então.

titleEn: The Oral, Parts I and II: Yourself and the Role-Play
titlePt: A Prova Oral, Partes I e II: Identificação e Simulação
blurbEn: You will be able to answer every predictable identity question in full sentences and handle a shop, a clinic or a ticket-office role-play without freezing.
grammarFocus: formas de tratamento — o examinador trata por 'você / o senhor', o candidato responde na 1.ª pessoa
notePrompt: Set the scene first: the oral lasts 10 to 15 minutes, is recorded on video, and CAPLE states it is held 'sempre que possível, com dois candidatos ao mesmo tempo', so the candidate is almost certainly examined beside a stranger they did not choose. Parte I is identificação pessoal and is entirely predictable, so rehearse it to fluency against the real question set: Como se chama? Pode soletrar o seu apelido, se faz favor? De onde é? Quantos anos tem? Onde é que mora? Há quanto tempo vive em Portugal? Com quem é que vive? O que faz? Onde aprendeu português? Há quanto tempo estuda português? Porque está a fazer este exame? Descreva um dia normal. O que gosta de fazer nos tempos livres? Warn about register in both directions: the examiner addresses the candidate FORMALLY in the third person without 'tu', which sounds like a he/she form and throws people, and the answer is always first person — 'Chamo-me…', 'Moro em Santa Cruz, perto de Torres Vedras', 'Vivo em Portugal há três anos', 'Estou a estudar português para pedir a nacionalidade'. Parte II is a simulation of a public or personal situation, and the reported task types are worth rehearsing one by one: buying bread and cakes, exchanging a faulty item with the talão, ordering a meal and asking for a conta, phoning to marcar uma consulta at the centro de saúde, asking about an apartment and the renda, buying a bus or train ticket (ida e volta), asking for directions, phoning the school because a child is ill, asking the junta de freguesia for an atestado de residência. Give one frame that covers them all: greeting, 'Queria…, se faz favor', a question ('Quanto custa?', 'A que horas é o próximo autocarro?', 'Posso trocá-la?'), a follow-up, then thanks — with one extra detail added to every turn, because one-word answers starve the examiner of evidence across every criterion at once. Teach the emergency formulas as scored interaction behaviour, not as failure: 'Desculpe, pode repetir, se faz favor?', 'Desculpe, não percebi. Pode explicar outra vez?', 'Deixe-me pensar um bocadinho…', 'Não sei a palavra em português, mas é uma coisa para…'. Insist on European forms, because accuracy is watched: estou a falar not estou falando, chamo-me not me chamo, autocarro, comboio, telemóvel, pequeno-almoço, casa de banho, os seus tempos livres. Be honest that CAPLE publishes no sample oral paper and no marking grid: the tasks above come from first-hand candidate accounts, and the criteria usually quoted (âmbito, correção, fluência, interação, coerência e coesão) are inferred from the CEFR and ALTE tradition CAPLE works within, not stated by CAPLE.

titleEn: The Oral, Part III: Talking With Your Partner
titlePt: A Prova Oral, Parte III: Falar a Dois
blurbEn: You will be able to hold the paired discussion — describe your picture, give an opinion, bring the other candidate in and disagree politely — instead of just waiting your turn.
notePrompt: Parte III is officially 'interação sobre um tópico relativo a acontecimentos da atualidade', but the first-hand accounts describe something gentler and far more rehearsable: a shared prompt the pair must discuss and settle together — a sheet of five professions to choose between, or seven holiday options to agree on — and, in several accounts, an individual photograph to describe for about two minutes, with each candidate getting a different image. This is the phase that carries the interaction mark and the phase almost nobody prepares, because everyone practises answering the examiner and nobody practises asking their partner a question. Teach four moves explicitly and require all four in every practice run: give an opinion with a reason ('Na minha opinião…', 'Prefiro… porque…', 'Acho que…', 'Para mim…'); bring the other person in ('E tu, o que achas?', 'Concordas comigo?'); disagree politely ('Boa ideia, mas eu prefiro…', 'Sim, mas por outro lado…', 'Tens razão, no entanto…'); and close on a decision ('Então vamos ao Alentejo?', 'Combinado.'). Build a bank of five topics the learner can say three sentences about, each with an opinion, a reason and an example — house prices and rents, public transport where they live, the weather and the seasons, telemóveis and redes sociais, and a Portuguese festa they have been to. Name the four ways candidates lose marks here: saying too little, going silent instead of asking for clarification, switching off while the partner is speaking so there is nothing to respond to, and monopolising a weaker partner, which demonstrates the absence of interaction rather than its presence. Reassure them on the two things they cannot control: examiners assess each candidate against the standard rather than against the partner, and struggling to understand the other candidate is a common, reported problem whose only mitigation is practising with several different speakers, not just one teacher. Remind them that pausing, false starts and reformulation are expected at A2 and are not in themselves errors — stopping is the only real failure, because silence produces no evidence to score. State clearly that CAPLE publishes no oral specimen and no marking grid, so everything above about what happens in the room comes from candidate reports and must be taught as likely, not as certain.

blurbEn: You will be able to sit the whole exam in the real order, on the real clocks, score it with the real weighting, and know exactly where your last week of study goes.
notePrompt: This unit is a rehearsal, and its subject is order and fatigue rather than content. Run the components in the sequence the day actually uses: the 75-minute written paper, a 15-minute break, then the 30-minute listening audio played straight through without pausing, then a paired speaking rehearsal of 10 to 15 minutes with a partner. Do the listening AFTER the written paper and never fresh, because thirty minutes of concentrated listening on a tired ear is the real condition — on the national sessions the written paper starts at 09h00 and the listening at 10h30. Use real materials: pencil and eraser for the reading and listening, a blue or black pen for the two texts, a home-made answer grid numbered 1 to 25 for the listening, and the phone in another room. Score it properly rather than impressionistically: convert each component to a percentage, apply 0,45 / 0,30 / 0,25, and compare the weighted total with 55%; for the listening, about 14 of 25 is roughly the pass line for that component and about 18 of 25 is roughly a Bom, assuming the equal item weighting that CAPLE does not publish. Then triage instead of re-studying everything: put the remaining days into whichever component moves the weighted total fastest, which for most adults already living in Portugal is reading, then speaking, and almost never grammar theory. Because CAPLE publishes no transcript of the model audio, add the highest-value follow-up available: after the timed run, transcribe the listening texts by ear, slowly and with pauses, and compare that with what you thought you heard — it shows why an item was missed, not merely that it was. Run the whole simulation twice, once around week eight and once in the final week, and compare the three component numbers rather than the total, because a total hides which paper is drifting. Finish by writing down the specific task types still failing by name, so the last week is a plan and not a panic.

blurbEn: You will be able to get yourself a seat, arrive with the right documents, and avoid the handful of rules that annul an entire exam.
notePrompt: Start with the thing that decides everything: the seat. Each LAPE (the local exam centre) decides for itself how many vagas to open, there is no national pool and no waiting list, and sittings sell out — Portuguese press reporting in late 2025 described immigrants travelling to Madrid to sit the Portuguese exam because places here were gone. Registration is done online at CAPLE in five steps (exam and country, centre, session, personal data, payment), needs the NIF and the ID number to hand, and allows only 24 hours to pay; miss that and there is a 48-hour lockout, during which the seat disappears. The fee is non-refundable and stood at 95 euros in 2026 on two independent LAPE pages, while a third still displayed an older 72 euros — CAPLE publishes no price table, so confirm the amount on screen before paying. Registration also requires consent to the video recording of the oral and a declaration of being 18 or over or holding parental authorisation; a school version, CIPLE-e, exists for candidates aged 12 to 15. Tactics that actually work: register on the day the window opens, at 15h00 sharp, with the card ready, and watch several centres at once — there are 21 LAPE in Portugal but none in Torres Vedras, Caldas da Rainha or Óbidos, so for a family near Santa Cruz the realistic set is the three Lisbon centres, Sintra and Leiria. The Lisbon Faculdade de Letras runs roughly monthly CIPLE sittings whose registration opens about five to seven weeks ahead and closes about two weeks before the exam, alongside the national sessions (in 2026 these fell in May, July and November); CAPLE publishes its calendar only as images, so check the épocas page rather than trusting a third-party date. Choose the session by counting BACKWARDS from the date the certificate is needed, not from the exam date: results have run roughly seven to eight weeks after the exam and certificates reach the centre roughly four weeks after results, so a November sitting can mean a certificate in February. On the day, arrive 20 minutes early with the ORIGINAL of the same identity document used at registration (cartão de cidadão, passaporte ou título de residência); more than 15 minutes late for the reading and writing paper and you are not admitted, and for the listening paper ANY lateness excludes you. Bring a blue or black pen plus pencil and eraser; phones, laptops, dictionaries, books, notebooks and correction fluid are forbidden; never write your name anywhere on the exam; hand back both the folha de respostas and the enunciado; stay until the scheduled end. Finally, the rules with teeth: missing any single component annuls the whole exam, a justified absence can be transferred to the next session once only if submitted in writing within five working days, and a re-check of the result costs 25 euros, must be requested within five working days of publication, and its decision is final.
